content_payload.front_text: First lesson: no review yet. Move to the next block.
content_payload.back_text: First lesson: no review yet. Move to the next block.

slides.teacher_cue: Introduce the phoneme-grapheme card routine. Explain that a letter makes a sound and every lesson begins by checking what students know.
slides.expected_response: Students attend to the routine and understand that print maps to sound.
slides.correction_move: Re-model with one example card and restate the routine simply.
slides.observation_note: Lesson 1 has no prior phonemes to review. This block establishes the routine only.

slides.teacher_cue: There are no prior words yet. Use this block to establish the encoding routine with single sound-to-letter practice.
slides.expected_response: Students attempt to hear one sound and write one matching letter.
slides.correction_move: Model one sound slowly, show how to write the matching grapheme, then repeat together.
slides.observation_note: Lesson 1 Block 02 is routine setup, not prior-word review.

slides.teacher_cue: Make a snake sound — ssssss. Feel the air on your hand.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /s/ as a steady hiss.
slides.correction_move: Model /s/ again with airflow emphasis, then repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Voiceless alveolar fricative. Tongue tip near the ridge behind the upper teeth. Air flows continuously.

slides.teacher_cue: Open your mouth wide like a doctor visit — aaaa.
slides.expected_response: Students produce short /æ/ with an open mouth and low tongue.
slides.correction_move: Model /æ/ again with a wider jaw drop and brief repetition.
slides.observation_note: Short open front vowel. Mouth open wide, tongue low and flat, jaw drops noticeably.

slides.teacher_cue: Tap the roof of your mouth and let it pop — t! t! t!
slides.expected_response: Students produce /t/ with a clean sharp release.
slides.correction_move: Model /t/ again and exaggerate the tongue tap and release.
slides.observation_note: Voiceless alveolar stop. Tongue tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth, builds pressure, then releases.

slides.teacher_cue: Sight word — underlined. Say it as a whole unit. It uses the /aɪ/ diphthong — not taught until Lesson 34. Use it in a short oral sentence: I sat. Then reveal.
slides.expected_response: Students say I orally and recognise it as a whole-unit sight word — not a blend.
slides.correction_move: Model I in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students try to blend I. Redirect — sight word, say it whole. I appears in Block 06 and Block 07 of this lesson.

slides.teacher_cue: Vocabulary warm-up. Say the word, connect meaning, then read it together.
slides.expected_response: Students read sat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the word, then repeat chorally and point to each part if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for smooth oral reading before it appears in connected text.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Introduce sat. Keep it oral first, then reveal print.
Model sat clearly once.
Choral response. Listen for clean word reading.

slides.teacher_cue: Teach sat orally first, then reveal print.
slides.expected_response: Students say sat and connect it to meaning/action.
slides.correction_move: Model sat, repeat chorally, then reveal the written word.
slides.observation_note: Word is decodable with the current pool s · a · t.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Introduce sat. Keep it oral first, then reveal print.
Model sat clearly once.
Choral response. Listen for clean word reading.

slides.teacher_cue: Teach at orally in a simple phrase, then reveal print.
slides.expected_response: Students say at and recognise it in context.
slides.correction_move: Model at in a short phrase, then repeat and reveal print.
slides.observation_note: Word is decodable with the current pool s · a · t.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Introduce at in a short phrase before print.
Model at clearly once.
Choral response. Listen for accurate word reading.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to the picture and model: a jar. Explain that a is used before one thing. Students repeat the phrase together.
slides.expected_response: Students recognise a as a high-frequency useful word.
slides.correction_move: Model a in a short phrase, then repeat and reveal print.
slides.observation_note: Sight word active this lesson alongside the and I.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Set meaning first. One thing only.
Model the phrase once.
Choral response. Confirm meaning and phrase reading.

slides.slide_title: Review today's sounds With Known Words
slides.teacher_cue: Read it, track the parts, and confirm that every part fits the taught pool for today's sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students read the word accurately and explain why it is safe to read.
slides.correction_move: Tap each sound or chunk, blend, then reread smoothly.
slides.observation_note: Use this as confidence-building cumulative review, not as a surprise challenge.

slides.teacher_cue: Build sat left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students blend and build sat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting /s/ /æ/ /t/, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: This block establishes the blending routine. Keep volume low and process explicit.

state_sequence.prompt: Check every sound. Mark the class.

slides.teacher_cue: Build at left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build at accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the sounds slowly, then rebuild.
slides.observation_note: Only three phonemes are available in Lesson 1, so the word list is intentionally short.

slides.teacher_cue: Build as left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build as accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the sounds slowly, then rebuild.
slides.observation_note: The focus is establishing the blending routine, not volume.

content_payload.prompt_text: Build the today's sounds word, read it, then rebuild it without help.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the today's sounds word once, read it, clear it, then rebuild it without help.
slides.expected_response: Students build, read, clear, and rebuild accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model one build slowly, then have students repeat with less support.
slides.observation_note: Watch for whether students are mapping parts to print or only recalling the shape.

slides.teacher_cue: Lesson 1 has only one meaningful sentence at this stage. Establish the sentence reading routine, not test volume.
slides.expected_response: Students read "I sat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model once, then track each word left to right and reread together.
slides.observation_note: Sight words active: the · a · I. Sentence uses I plus sat.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Set tracking and sentence focus.
Model the sentence once with tracking.
Choral read. Confirm tracking and accuracy.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What does this tell you about the sounds? Say it back in your own words.

slides.teacher_cue: Read it smoothly, then explain the sentence in your own words.
slides.expected_response: Students read accurately and explain the meaning of the s, a, t sentence.
slides.correction_move: Reread in a phrase, then prompt for a brief retell or answer.
slides.observation_note: Push comprehension right after decoding so the focus does not stay mechanical.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Keep meaning tied to the sentence.
Choral read before explanation.
Take one or two oral explanations, then mark the class.

comprehension_questions: What does it mean to sit or sat?
Use sat in your own sentence.

slides.teacher_cue: Keep the text stable. Luminos runs the reading roster first, then fluency support, then mixed comprehension turns on the same slide.
slides.expected_response: Students read the sentence, reread when needed, and then answer the mixed comprehension prompts.
slides.correction_move: Echo read first, then repeat while pointing to each word. Use the comprehension round only after every student has had a reading turn.
slides.observation_note: Lesson 1 reader is a single-sentence runtime. Do not advance to a new slide for reread or comprehension when the text has not changed.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate sat. Students segment into phonemes using Elkonin boxes, then write.
slides.expected_response: Students write sat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat sat, segment /s/ /æ/ /t/, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Reveal and check after writing.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate at. Students segment into phonemes using Elkonin boxes, then write.
slides.expected_response: Students write at accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat at, segment /æ/ /t/, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Reveal and check after writing.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate a. Students write the word after hearing it.
slides.expected_response: Students write a accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the word again, then rewrite and check.
slides.observation_note: Block 08 words are drawn from Block 04 vocabulary.

slides.slide_title: Write today's sounds And Read Back

content_payload.prompt_text: Write the today's sounds target from memory. Then read it back and check every part.

slides.teacher_cue: Write the today's sounds target carefully from memory, then read it back aloud and check every part.
slides.expected_response: Students write accurately and read back what they wrote.
slides.correction_move: Prompt students to say each sound or chunk as they check their writing.
slides.observation_note: The goal is accurate encoding plus immediate self-checking.

content_payload.support_text: What do you notice? Which sound part do they share?

slides.teacher_cue: Draw attention to sat and at. Keep it informal — no metalinguistic terminology required.
slides.expected_response: Students notice the shared /æ/ · /t/ pattern.
slides.correction_move: Read both words, point to at, and repeat the shared part.
slides.observation_note: Group 1 Morpheme Moment is light pattern noticing only.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Direct attention to both printed words.
Elicit the shared ending and then advance.

content_payload.support_text: Both words share the -at ending. What does at mean? How does adding s- change sat from just at?

slides.teacher_cue: Guide students to see the semantic connection — at is a place word; sat tells us what happened there.
slides.expected_response: Students explain that at tells where, and sat tells what happened.
slides.correction_move: Model one explanation, then ask students to describe the others.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can articulate meaning, not just form.

slides.slide_title: Use today's sounds In New Speech

content_payload.support_text: Say a full sentence with one of these sounds. Then change one part and say a new sentence.

slides.teacher_cue: Use today's sounds in one full sentence. Then change one part and say a second sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students produce one complete sentence and then extend or vary it.
slides.correction_move: Model one sentence, then prompt for a second sentence with one changed word or part.
slides.observation_note: Push for full oral language, not one-word answers.

state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Shift from pattern noticing to meaning.

state_sequence.board_prompt: What does at mean? How is sat different?
state_sequence.teacher_prompt: Take one or two oral answers, then mark the class.
state_sequence.tts_prompt: What does at mean? How is sat different?

content_payload.title: Close the Lesson

check_items.label: We learned three sounds today: s, a, t.
What did I do? Can you show me?
Tell me one full sentence using I or sat.

content_payload.notes_field: Keep the close brief, oral, and text-based.

slides.teacher_cue: Close with pattern recall, meaning from the reader, and one brief oral transfer sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students answer orally, refer back to the reader when needed, and produce one full sentence with lesson vocabulary.
slides.correction_move: Return to the reader, point to the relevant sentence, then model one full oral answer.
slides.observation_note: Watch for pattern recall, text-based answers, and whether the final oral sentence stays accurate and complete.

slides.teacher_cue: Show the sentence starter. Students complete it in writing using lesson words. They may use any decodable word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students write a complete, accurate sentence using at least one word from the lesson.
slides.correction_move: Model one example sentence aloud, then students try again independently.
slides.observation_note: Watch spelling accuracy on lesson vocabulary words and whether the sentence is grammatically complete.

content_payload.support_text: Say one final strong sentence using today's today's sounds focus.

slides.teacher_cue: Give me one more full sentence or idea using today's sounds focus before we finish.
slides.expected_response: Students give one final complete sentence or idea connected to the lesson focus.
slides.correction_move: If needed, model the start of a sentence and have students finish it clearly.
slides.observation_note: End with a strong oral response so the lesson closes on language and meaning.
